grammar.label: the historic present in reportage and summary
grammar.form: present simple for past events, sustained across a passage
grammar.meaning: brings a past narrative or a written source into the reader's present

explanation.en: 'In chapter three, Karimova turns to the border villages.' A book always argues in the present. A news narrative may shift into the present at the dramatic moment and back out afterwards. The rule is consistency: a passage that drifts between past and present without a reason reads as carelessness, not as style.
explanation.uz: 'In chapter three, Karimova turns to the border villages.' Kitob doim hozirgi zamonda bahs yuritadi. Qoida — izchillik: sababsiz zamondan zamonga o'tish uslub emas, e'tiborsizlik sifatida o'qiladi.

grammar.positive_example: Halfway through the novel the narrator stops trusting his own account.
grammar.negative_example: Halfway through the novel the narrator stopped trusting his own account, and then tells us why.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida hikoyani hozirgi zamonda aytish odatiy, lekin akademik iqtibos uchun bu qoida yangi.

grammar.label: tense shift as a signal of distance and stance
grammar.form: moving between past, present and would within one passage
grammar.meaning: marks how close the writer stands to what is being reported

explanation.en: A shift of tense can move the reader without any explicit signal. 'He said the road was finished' reports; 'he said the road is finished' keeps the claim live and, by implication, endorses it. 'The road would be finished by June' inside a past narrative is the future-in-the-past. At C1 these shifts are read as stance, so an accidental one makes a claim the writer did not intend.
explanation.uz: Zamonning o'zgarishi hech qanday qo'shimcha belgisiz o'quvchini siljitadi. 'He said the road is finished' — da'vo hamon kuchda va yozuvchi unga qo'shiladi.

grammar.positive_example: She insisted the figures were wrong; they are, as it turns out, wrong.
grammar.negative_example: She insisted the figures are wrong; they were, as it turns out, wrong.

l1_notes.uz: Rus tilida bilvosita nutqda zamon o'zgarmaydi, shuning uchun ingliz tilidagi backshift muntazam xato manbai.

body.text: 'In chapter three Karimova turned to the border villages.'

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Turns. The book is still doing it.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: And the argument is on the page this morning. That is why we cite in the present.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: So the past tense is for what she did and the present is for what the book does.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Exactly that. 'She spent two winters in the villages' — past. 'She argues that the road came too late' — present.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: My second paragraph drifts between the two.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Then fix the paragraph, not the rule. Drifting reads as carelessness even when the reader cannot say why.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: There is one more. I wrote 'she said the road is finished'.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Do you agree that it is finished?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Then 'was'. Keeping the present puts your name behind her claim, and you did not mean to lend it.
